title: World War II Expedition
tagline: Recover the story. Connect the events.
scope: An interactive archive of selected military turning points, not a complete account of WWII. The map is schematic, not geographic.
goals: Explain how events changed the course of the war.

discoveries.title: Invasion of Poland
discoveries.summary: Germany invaded Poland. Britain and France declared war two days later, widening the European conflict.

question.prompt: Which response widened the war after Germany invaded Poland?
choices: Britain and France declared war
The United States declared war on Japan
Japan surrendered
The Normandy landings began
question.explanation: Britain and France honored their guarantee to Poland.

discoveries.title: Battle of Britain
discoveries.summary: Britain resisted Germany’s air offensive. Germany did not gain the air superiority needed for its planned invasion.

question.prompt: What did Britain’s resistance help prevent?
choices: A German invasion of Britain
Germany’s invasion of Poland
The attack on Pearl Harbor
The Soviet capture of Berlin
question.explanation: Britain remained in the war rather than falling to a German invasion.

discoveries.title: Invasion of the Soviet Union
discoveries.summary: Germany attacked the Soviet Union, beginning a vast Eastern Front that demanded forces and supplies.

question.prompt: How did this invasion change Germany’s war?
choices: It opened a major Eastern Front
It ended the war in Europe
It brought Japan into NATO
It removed the need for supplies
question.explanation: Germany now faced a prolonged struggle in the east as well as its other commitments.

connection.prompt: Connect the discoveries: why did the invasion of the Soviet Union expand the conflict?
choices: Germany opened a vast new front while Britain remained undefeated
Britain and Germany became allies
All European fighting moved to the Pacific
The Soviet Union had already surrendered
connection.explanation: A new front expanded the territory, resources, and opponents involved.

discoveries.title: Pearl Harbor
discoveries.summary: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor. The United States declared war on Japan the following day.

question.prompt: What followed the attack on Pearl Harbor?
choices: The United States declared war on Japan
The war in Europe ended
Germany invaded Poland
Japan formally surrendered
question.explanation: The attack brought the United States into open war with Japan.

discoveries.title: Battle of Midway
discoveries.summary: U.S. forces destroyed four Japanese aircraft carriers, weakening Japan’s ability to conduct carrier operations.

question.prompt: Why was Midway a turning point?
choices: Japan lost four aircraft carriers
It ended all Pacific fighting immediately
It caused Germany’s surrender
It began the war in Europe
question.explanation: Carrier losses weakened Japanese naval power; the war continued.

discoveries.title: Guadalcanal campaign
discoveries.summary: Allied forces fought to hold Guadalcanal’s airfield. Their success helped protect supply routes and begin a sustained advance.

question.prompt: What did Allied success at Guadalcanal support?
choices: Protected supply routes and further advances
Immediate peace with Japan
A German invasion of Britain
The start of the Polish campaign
question.explanation: Control of the airfield helped secure routes toward Australia and New Zealand.

choices: The Allies moved from checking Japanese expansion toward taking the initiative
Both battles immediately ended the war
Both took place on the Eastern Front
Both occurred before Pearl Harbor
connection.explanation: Midway weakened Japanese carrier power; Guadalcanal helped the Allies advance.

discoveries.title: Stalingrad surrender
discoveries.summary: Encircled German forces surrendered at Stalingrad, marking a major defeat on the Eastern Front.

question.prompt: Which theater did the defeat at Stalingrad affect?
choices: The European Eastern Front
The central Pacific
The Atlantic coast of North America
The Normandy beaches
question.explanation: Stalingrad was a major defeat for Germany in the Soviet Union.

discoveries.title: Normandy landings
discoveries.summary: Allied landings in France established a foothold for the liberation of Western Europe. Months of fighting followed.

question.prompt: How did D-Day contribute to Germany’s defeat?
choices: It established a western foothold while fighting continued in the east
It ended all fighting that day
It started the war in Europe
It brought Germany and Britain into an alliance
question.explanation: The landings supported a westward-to-eastward Allied advance across occupied Western Europe.

discoveries.title: V-E Day
discoveries.summary: Germany’s surrender took effect in Europe. The Pacific war continued until Japan’s surrender later in 1945.

question.prompt: What distinction matters when describing V-E Day?
choices: The European war ended; the Pacific war continued
All worldwide fighting ended that day
Japan surrendered before Pearl Harbor
The European war had not begun
question.explanation: Victory in Europe did not mark the end of the Pacific war.

connection.prompt: How did Allied advances in the east and west relate to Germany’s defeat?
choices: Germany faced pressure from multiple directions
Every Allied army used the same route
The Pacific war ended before Germany surrendered
D-Day removed the Eastern Front
connection.explanation: Soviet advances and the western Allied campaign both contributed to Germany’s defeat.

finalPrompt: Choose two connected discoveries. Explain how they show a change in the course of the war. Use a specific detail from each.
